metaData.title: AI Can Use Any Means to Write Anything, But You Must Be a "Veteran Engineer"
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Through interviews with industry experts like Huang Dongxu, Xu Hao, and Teng Yu, this article explores the capability boundaries of AI Agents in software development, pointing out that AI can already write almost any software, but human judgment and knowledge management remain the core value, while also analyzing practical challenges such as the deconstruction of tech stack lock-in, declining rewrite costs, and enterprise software maintenance.
metaData.summary: Using PingCAP CTO Huang Dongxu's db9 project as a starting point, this article reveals the astonishing capabilities of AI Agents in software development: completing a database project with 1 million lines of Rust code in three months with zero human coding. Centered around the premise that "AI can write anything," the article discusses the phenomenon of tech stack lock-ins (language, framework, database) being broken—Bun migrated from Zig to Rust in just 6 days, and enterprises can use Agents to rewrite applications at any time. It then explores the trend of "rewriting," including the restoration of sourceless systems (the Thoughtworks case, the rebuilding of a 30-year-old MUD game), and points out that what truly matters is the knowledge within the software rather than the code itself. Xu Hao emphasizes knowledge engineering, arguing that the essence of development is specifying specifications and acceptance criteria, with AI acting merely as a "compiler" to transform the carrier. The article finally focuses on human value: the steering and judgment of senior engineers ("veterans") are irreplaceable, while enterprise software maintenance remains a pain point, as AI-generated code might introduce more bugs after deployment. The entire article features exclusive interviews with multiple experts, offering substantial information and sharp insights.

mainPoints.point: AI Agents can already write almost any type of software, with no obvious boundaries in sight.
mainPoints.explanation: Huang Dongxu's db9 project (1 million lines of Rust database code) proves that with a reasonable harness and collaborative approach, AI can produce complex, production-ready code at extremely low costs and speeds far exceeding human teams.

mainPoints.point: Tech stack lock-in is being broken, and rewrite costs are dropping drastically.
mainPoints.explanation: Language, framework, and database choices no longer constitute long-term lock-ins; Bun migrated from Zig to Rust in just 6 days, and enterprises believe that wrong decisions can be reversed using Agents. Agents have no taste preferences; they only care about interfaces and documentation.

mainPoints.point: The code itself is not the product; the knowledge within the software is the core competitiveness.
mainPoints.explanation: Xu Hao points out that what is truly valuable is the specifications, rules, and business logic沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀沉淀 in the software, rather than the implementation carrier; AI acts like a compiler, migrating knowledge across different tech stacks.

mainPoints.point: Human value lies in steering and judgment; senior engineers ("veterans") are more important than ever.
mainPoints.explanation: AI only seeks to please and lacks a sense of direction; experienced individuals are needed to define architectures, set constraints, and verify outputs. Programmers who merely write code will be eliminated, while those who can deliver value are presented with the best opportunity.

mainPoints.point: Enterprise software maintenance remains a practical challenge, and AI code may bring new problems.
mainPoints.explanation: Issues such as the "spaghetti code" of legacy systems, semantic detail incompatibilities, and a surge in bugs after deployment make fully relying on AI for rewrites still unfeasible; ultimately, humans must still bear the responsibility.

keyQuotes: I have now fallen into a massive nihilism; AI can write anything.
AI can basically use any solution, any tool, any means to write anything.
What is truly useful is not the code itself, but the knowledge precipitated in the software—documentation, legacy rules, business logic, and system behavior.
If a person believes their job is just to write code, that person should have been eliminated by the industry long ago, even without the emergence of AI today.
Those taste wars that make humans fight to the death simply do not exist for Agents.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Tencent Wang Tengfei: From Generating Content to Generating Environments - The 3D Implementation Path of World Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This is an in-depth interview with Wang Tengfei, head of Tencent's Hunyuan World Model team, explaining the core differences between world models and video generation/3D generation, breaking down the four-stage generation process of HY-World 2.0, and discussing the 3D implementation path, its relationship with gaming/embodied intelligence, and open-source ecosystem directions.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Life of a Token: Understanding How Large Models Generate Tokens Like Debugging Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Using the GPT-2 Small model as an example, this article traces the complete inference process for a specific input 'The capital of France is', dissecting each step of data transformation in the Transformer model—from tokenization and word embedding to self-attention, feed-forward networks, and final prediction—revealing the internal mechanisms of LLM token generation.

relatedArticles.title: When Agents Truly Enter Complex Data Analysis Scenarios: DataClawBench Uses 492 Real-World Tasks for a Process-Level Examination of Frontier Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: DataClawBench is a data analysis evaluation benchmark based on 492 real-world financial think tank tasks. By retaining uncleaned data and hiding data source priors, it conducts a process-level evaluation of frontier large models, revealing their capability boundaries and failure modes in real exploratory analysis scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: GLM-5.1 Open Source: A Model Capable of 8 Hours of Independent Work
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Zhipu AI releases its flagship model GLM-5.1, featuring breakthrough Long-Horizon Task capabilities that allow it to work independently for 8 hours and deliver engineering-grade results.

relatedArticles.title: Stock Soars 735% with AI, Company Begins Mass Layoffs of Replaceable Roles, All Hires Require CEO Approval
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AppLovin CEO Adam Foroughi shares an in-depth interview on the company's turnaround from a 92% stock crash to a $140 billion market cap, along with his unique management philosophy of extreme simplicity, AI-driven operations, and hiring only A-players.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: From Rejecting AI to Asking Agent First for Everything: DHH Says It's One of His Most Enjoyable Programming Moments, But the Golden Age for Programmers Is Ending
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Ruby on Rails creator DHH shares his shift from resisting AI to fully embracing an Agent-First programming workflow, believing AI is amplifying the value of senior engineers, but the 'golden age' for programmers may be coming to an end.
